Source: lodge-docs/PLAYER-GUIDE-full.md, Part 2

A Keystone (the character sheet also calls it a Quirk) is a permanent, one-of-a-kind foundation — the thing about your character that no amount of play changes. Usually that foundation is a graft, the surgery that made you a Ripper in the first place; but an inherited relic, a rival, a debt, or another foundational truth about who you are qualifies just as well. Unlike a Guise, which is worn and swapped, the Keystone is in you. It survives every mask change and every disguise.

> One Keystone per Ripper, ever. No two alike at a table. NPCs hold none.

  • Taken at character creation, or at the moment the surgery happens in play. Never two at once.
  • Want a second? You lose the first. The table narrates a revision surgery.
  • Everything grafted afterwards is a narrative Trait — flavour and story, available to anyone, not a mechanical Keystone.
  • The Vampyre commits your Keystone to Revenant. That class makes the choice for you, and it exhausts your entire affinity allowance on what you are.

Available Keystones

34 are in play at this table.

KeystoneEffectCost / hook
AgitatorOn a rest, learn what the locals are angry about or afraid ofA history, not a graft — but the knowledge arrives reliably
THE ATTAINTEDAbsorption to one chosen damage type + Vulnerability to its pair; Ritualism for that elementAbsorb air→bolt · bolt→earth · dark→light · earth→air · fire→ice · ice→fire · poison→fire. Absorption counts as two Immunities — Guises grant nothing
Big BroInstalls Camp Activities even if the group doesn't otherwise use them; three activities, two per rest — including Daydream (halve an HP loss) and Exploration (on a 6, level × 50z)Activities fire on resting scenes, which are gated by Limited Resting Scenes
THE CLAIMANTThe printed Glorious Fate benefits, minus a prophecyYou are not chosen — you are designated, and the designation has consequences whether or not it is true
Cognitive GhostTwo Resistances, one Vulnerability; Ritualism for Aether transit, information and trackingThe Ritualism is already scoped and refunds nothing from the pool
THE CREWYour character is a group treated as one creature — HP losses are members falling, recovery is members rejoining. One for All: Resistance to all damage types from single-target sources, Vulnerability to all types from anything hitting three or more creatures at onceDamage with no type ignores both Affinities normally — an untyped strike goes straight through. Decide at session zero who the Crew is (Dockers, a household, the Irregulars)
CursedBefore any Check, describe how the curse interferes and automatically fumble — earn 2 Fabula Points instead of 1, and generate an opportunity as normalThe largest player-side Miasma faucet in the game. Uncapped by design. Breaking the Curse is tied to resolving a world threat. Declare this at session zero, not in play
Elemental SoulResistance to one damage type, Vulnerability to another; Elementalism for that element onlyReskin as one specific monster's aether grafted deep — not an abstract element
Guardian of Light/Shadow (Elemental Soul variant)Elemental Soul, but in light or dark, with Entropism instead of ElementalismThe dark option is a lesser Revenant — Resistance rather than Immunity
Empty Hands+1 Defence and +1 Magic Defence (flat)Conflicts with the Hunter Weapon — a character with Empty Hands has no use for the two-handed slot
Fettered HeartWrite three commandments of your own at creation. On the sixth violation, you are broken open and revealed. After the endgame consequence: +1 to all Bond strengthsThe Lodge trio (always answer a Lodge summons · never reveal a graft to an outsider · never let a monster live) is one example, not a requirement. The +1 does not stack with the Tell's
Fugitive ExperimentIgnore any HP, MP or IP cost of ≤100, anywhere; gain 1d8 Instability per use, losing 1d6 per session; at 10+ Instability you drop to 0 HP and must SurrenderRoughly one use a session at low risk, dangerous at two, a forced Surrender at three. The only cost-ignorer that can pay a Ritual cost. Your breakdown ticks the Miasma Clock
Heads-Up DisplayOne level of Quick Assessment at no MP cost; with Quick Assessment from another source, treat it as if 5 more MP were spentPressure points count as Traits — this is one free pressure-point reveal at the start of every conflict, from level one
HeirloomA 1200z-equivalent accessory, or any two common clots, that cannot be lost or stolen; earn 1 FP when rivals or monsters are drawn to itNo Keystone grants a weapon. The FP is wrong-way — it ticks the Clock
Hundred FacesA disguise that fools soldiers reliably; pierced by an elite's Check or a Villain spending 1 Ultima PointDoes not cover the Tell
Inventor ProdigySpend 1 FP to declare you have the required special ingredient; ignore IP costs once per conflict scene"Begin Projects" is struck — you still need a pool pick for Projects. The FP is wrong-way
Mysterious GrimoireA book that answers one question per session when you begin investigating a new site; endgame branch: Hidden MagicTrigger was moved off travel rolls. The Awakened Consciousness branch (free NPC caster) is cut
Neo-HumanWith a base d12 in an Attribute, treat it as d20 on any Check using that Attribute — at will — and the GM gains an opportunity each timeCheck-only; never Defence, Magic Defence, HP or MP. The opportunity rider is the price
Nether DelinquentAccumulate Delinquency Points through good acts; they make you hit harder and be hit harder; spend them with a selfish act for a Fabula PointEngine kept; Infernal Academy discarded
Old TransportA party-sized vehicle explicitly unfit for combat; earn 2 FP when engines fail or the hull is damagedA carriage that breaks down in Whitechapel makes Whitechapel worse, twice over
Outcast FairyRitualism for transit to the Realm only; a unique weakness the GM may invoke for 1 FP, or you simply auto-fail a CheckCold iron is the fey's bane — and Foundry ammunition is iron. A character arc for free
THE PROMISE THAT BINDS YOUTheme locked to Guilt or Duty; +5 max HP and MP; one NPC spell (Cursed Breath, Life Theft, or Mind Theft — 10 MP, one creature, HR+15 of a chosen type, plus a status or drain rider). The break: 999 damage to each target, ignoring all Affinities. Any Villains among them stop being Villains and lose all Ultima Points. You become a Supreme Villain and roll a new characterGATE 1: a Villain must be among the targets. GATE 2: GM and player agree in advance that this is on the table. When the Promise breaks, the local Miasma Clock fills by 3 — and then ticks on the ordinary schedule forever
THE RATIONALISTOnce per scene, when a supernatural effect would apply to you, declare that it simply does not happen. Each use fills one section of your 4-section Denial clock. When Denial fills, the next supernatural effect applies twice, then the clock clearsThe setting's metaphysics make a genuine refusal to believe mechanically real — belief is load-bearing here
Repentant EnforcerRequires Theme Doubt or Guilt; creates a named Villain organisation with three strategies; spend 1 Subversion Point in place of 1 Fabula Point; a rare item in the Hunter Weapon slot; +10 HP and +10 MP on the organisation's defeatOne Subversion Point pays one Fabula Point — a discount, not free substitution
Revenant (Vampyre-committed)Not a living creature; Immunity dark + poison; Vulnerability light; immune to poisoned; no breathing, eating or drinking, normal resting and recovery; whenever you deal damage, you may change its type to dark; all dark damage ignores Immunities and ResistancesUses both your Immunity slots. Guises grant nothing while you hold it. The Vampyre makes this choice for you
Rival ProdigiesName your eternal rival — they become a minor Villain (5 Ultima Points) and you take a Bond of admiration or inferiority. While the rival is present and holds 1+ Ultima Points, any Check you fail is automatically a fumble (no reroll) and you earn 1 FP. Ignore HP/MP costs in one chosen specialisation for 1 FP per useThe rival's presence ticks the Clock once per scene, not once per fumble. You author a Villain and your own path to unmasking it — at Prosperity 20+, Villains spend double Ultima Points, draining your rival faster
Robot — THE AUTOMATONImmunity poison; Resistance earth; Vulnerability bolt; immune poisoned; not living; +2 to Checks involving machines, technology and constructsClockwork, dynamo, Foundry-work. Wires and coils; a thing that shorts
Robot — THE CREATUREAbsorption bolt; Vulnerability fire; immune poisoned; not living; +2 to three categories of your choosingAbsorption counts as two — sits exactly at the ceiling; Guises grant nothing. Fire is what a mob does — Rippertech is a secret and everybody already knows how to kill the Creature
Reincarnated as an Object (Robot variant — Creature build already uses it)Robot, but the fixed +2 categories become three of your choosingStrictly wider than THE AUTOMATON in 1892
THE RUINName the catastrophe you are supposed to bring — it becomes a world threat. When any rule requires you to spend HP, MP or Fabula Points, you may instead fill one section of the local Miasma Clock and describe the omens; that cost is waived. At the end of each session, roll 2d20 — at or below your character level, fill a section where you are (automatic at level 40+). Count every section filled this way across every district. On the ninth, you lose this Keystone and the thing you named happens. You cannot Sacrifice yourself until it doesThe counter is the sum of what you did to every district — spreading the cost across four boroughs still arrives at nine. Invoking a Bond is free (no FP cost = no Miasma tick)
Souls EntwinedTwo souls in one body — the graft carries a dead Ripper's soul belonging to another player's character. The Survive branch grants +10 HP and +10 MP; Final Farewell at the endRequires two committed players and a GM who will give the passenger scenes
Stubborn ScionTwo bodyguards always somehow present. Be careful! — when you suffer damage, you may halve it; costs 1d6 Fatigue from a shared 10-point pool, recovering 1d6 per sessionThe halving is untyped and unconditional — applies to bane, Vulnerability and untyped damage. Roughly two to three uses a session from level one
Survivor+5 max HP and MP, or +2 IP; one NPC spell; optionally, a martial proficiencyMartial proficiency is irrelevant in this ruleset. Refunds an uncontested pool pick
TalentedChoose two Specialties as though you hold two levels of the Outlander's SkilledSpecialties branch only. The Innate Guise grants two Specialties already — this doubles them to four
Traveling WorkshopSpend 1 FP to declare you have the required special ingredient for a Project or quick craft; gated behind Gourmet or TinkererNot a Projects refund. Got better under Cinematic Projects, where quick Projects need an ingredient every time
UnderchildIgnore any HP, MP or IP cost of ≤100 during a conflict, once per rest. When you meet a contraption or creature connected to ancient technology or a ruin's past, ask the GM one of: its purpose / what can activate it / what can deactivate it — truthful answer, and you describe a brief flashback. After the sixth answer, you remember why you were left dormant and the GM gives a key clue to an existing threat or reveals a new oneConflict-only (cannot pay a Ritual or Project). The revelation clock points straight at the Medjay's sites and whatever the Foundry built before anyone alive
